A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EnvPoser and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and supplementary Sections A–E. Corresponding content can be reliably matched despite minor edits and layout changes.

before.justification: Section 4 and supplementary Sections C–D report original EnvPoser evaluations, ablations, and qualitative results on EgoBody, GIMO, and self-collected VR data.

after.justification: v2 retains the original EnvPoser benchmark results, ablations, and qualitative demonstrations in the main text and supplementary material.

M1.justification: The uncertainty-aware estimation, sampling, environment refinement, contact prediction, and training losses are unchanged. Section 3.1 newly identifies the existing 132-dimensional output as 22 SMPL joints with 6D rotations; this is clarification, not evidence of a model change.

E1.justification: Both versions use AMASS for initial training, EgoBody and GIMO for motion-environment experiments, and self-collected VR data for qualitative validation. The evaluated scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain AvatarPoser, AGRoL, AvatarJLM, and S2Fusion, including the S2Fusion* reproduction on EgoBody. Comparator membership in the quantitative and qualitative comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported dataset splits, training procedures, 40-frame windows, scene sampling settings, and MPJRE, MPJPE, MPJVE, and Jitter metrics remain unchanged. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The semantic/geometric refinement and uncertainty ablations are retained. Supplementary Section C preserves the sampling and contact ablations and lower-body error analysis; Section D retains the same qualitative cases.

E5.justification: The supplementary lower-body MPJPE box plot and its reporting remain unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the model's uncertainty estimation is also retained.

E6.justification: The main and supplementary tables retain their numerical results, and the qualitative examples and findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports EnvPoser MPJPE of 74.7 mm on EgoBody and 57.6 mm on GIMO in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, sampling expression, and Equations (1)–(12) are unchanged. The added SMPL representation description supplies implementation context without introducing a new derivation, formal property, or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same two-stage uncertainty-aware, environment-aware framework and state-of-the-art performance on two public datasets. The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific scope.

C2.justification: The interpretations of environmental refinement and uncertainty modeling remain the same. The conclusion and supplementary Section E retain the limitations concerning static environments, moving objects and users, mesh quality, and reliance on pre-scanned geometry.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 newly specifies the first 22 SMPL joints and their 6D rotation representation. v2 also replaces the promised post-acceptance code-release footnote with a project-page pointer; the PDFs do not establish whether code is available there.

R1.justification: v2 adds Loper et al.'s SMPL paper as reference [26] to support the clarified pose representation. The remaining cited works and substantive positioning are retained; subsequent citation renumbering is incidental.

P1.justification: v2 compresses part of the introduction, makes small paragraph and wording edits, and clarifies the problem statement. Author roles and affiliations are updated and a funding acknowledgement is added, while the section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Supplementary Figure 1 and Table 1 move from PDF page 13 to page 12, with other appendix figures and tables repositioned through reflow. Printed page numbers are removed, but the figure/table inventory and overall two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit explanation of the 132-dimensional pose representation resolves a small documentation gap, while the SMPL citation and project-page pointer improve attribution and resource discoverability. These are limited gains: the method, experimental evidence, results, and substantive limitations remain unchanged, and code availability is not established by the PDFs.
